title: Dhurandhar Actress Ayesha Khan Says She Was 'Pushed Into a Van' by Mumbai Police During Student Protest
excerpt: Khan shared video of the incident, alleging she was detained without explanation while attempting to show solidarity with NEET protesters in Dadar.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ayesha Khan alleges she was forcibly detained by Mumbai Police during NEET protests.
  • Khan was surrounded by 15 officers and pushed into a police van.
  • Over 50 individuals have faced police action related to NEET protests in Mumbai.
  • Protests demand the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
  • Khan's situation highlights concerns over the right to peaceful assembly.

Actor Ayesha Khan, known for her appearance in the song "Shararat" from the Bollywood film Dhurandhar and her stint on Bigg Boss 17, has alleged that she was forcibly detained by Mumbai Police on Wednesday while attempting to join student protests in the Dadar neighbourhood.

In a video posted on Instagram, Khan recounted arriving at the protest site around 4 PM with her brother and friends to express solidarity with ongoing demonstrations against the NEET examination crisis. Before she could participate or display any slogans, she said, a police officer told her group that protesting at that location was not permitted.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=4463WHs_0VA

'I Used All My Strength to Not Get Into the Van'

When Khan asked about alternatives, the situation escalated rapidly. She described being surrounded by approximately 15 officers — both male and female — who ordered the group into a police van. "I was pulled by four or five women officers. I used all my strength to try not getting into the van, but they pulled us in," she said in her account.

> **""I was pulled by four or five women officers."**

In a separate post, Khan shared footage showing her being pushed into the vehicle, writing in the caption: "Today will be the most peaceful sleep of my life. I stood for what was right. Still in the police station asking the same question — why am I detained? Which law did I break?"

According to Khan, she and her companions repeatedly asked officers inside the van why they were being held but received no answers. The group was taken from Dadar to the Worli police station, where she said officers were more respectful, though she said no explanation was offered for the initial detention.

![Mumbai. Key Takeaways Ayesha Khan alleges she was forcibly detained by Mumbai Police during NEET protests.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/2b/Mumbai_Bandra-Worli_Sea_Link.jpg)

Part of a Wider Crackdown

Khan's detention is part of a broader police response to NEET-related protests that have spread across Indian cities. In Mumbai alone, police have filed cases against more than 50 individuals in connection with demonstrations at Chaityabhoomi and other locations. Several protesters have alleged they were detained without justification while peacefully assembling.

The protests in Mumbai are linked to a larger movement initiated by the Citizens for Justice and Peace (CJP) as a civil society action. The demonstrations, now in their third day in Mumbai and spreading to other cities, are demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and structural reform of the National Testing Agency.

Political figures including Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi have also been briefly detained during separate NEET-related demonstrations, while Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Thalapathy Vijay issued a public statement urging the government to "honour the feelings of students."

'Why Has Standing on the Street Become a Crime?'

Khan's account has drawn significant attention online, partly because of her public profile and partly because of the visual evidence she provided. Her question — "Why has standing on the street become a crime?" — has been widely shared as a summation of the frustrations felt by protesters who say their right to peaceful assembly is being curtailed.

Public Reaction and Concerns
›Khan's video of detention went viral.
›Criticism of police's heavy-handed tactics.
›Concerns over constitutional rights to assembly.
›Khan's question: 'Why has standing on the street become a crime?'

Mumbai Police have not issued a specific response to Khan's allegations. The broader policing approach to the protests has drawn criticism from civil liberties organisations, which argue that heavy-handed measures against peaceful demonstrators undermine constitutional guarantees of free expression and assembly.

Khan, whose acting career began with the TV show Balveer Returns before she gained wider recognition through Bigg Boss 17, has since appeared in several Hindi and Telugu productions. She is reportedly set to appear alongside Akshay Kumar in Bhagam Bhag 2.
